title: 150. 对英伟达研究副总裁刘洺堉的 4 小时访谈
title_en: A 4-Hour Interview with Ming-Yu Liu, NVIDIA's VP of Research
summary_cn: 一句话概括：英伟达第一位从研究员擢升至副总裁的管理者刘洺堉，在黄仁勋访华后一个月接受张小珺的 4 小时深谈。他讲透了英伟达的赌注哲学——押注物理世界 AI（Physical AI）、「zero-billion-dollar business」（可以不赚钱，但成功时必须极有影响力）、造市场而非存量竞争；也讲了如何在算力公司为研究争取 GPU、如何从研究员成长为 VP、Cosmos 世界模型从 22 个模型收敛到单一 Omni 模型的历程。最后他用中国功夫作答：「中国武术最重要的是控制自己，而不是展现破坏力」——模型竞争不应该是鱿鱼游戏
summary_en: Ming-Yu Liu, NVIDIA's first VP promoted from the research track, sits down with Zhang Xiaojun for a four-hour deep dive a month after Jensen Huang's China visit. He lays out NVIDIA's bet: Physical AI, the 'zero-billion-dollar business' (fine to make no money now, but it must be wildly influential if it succeeds), and building markets instead of fighting over existing ones. He also explains how to win GPUs for research inside a compute company, how to grow from researcher to VP, and how Cosmos collapsed from 22 models into a single Omni model. He closes with Chinese martial arts: 'the most important thing in kung fu is controlling yourself, not showing destructive power' — model competition shouldn't be a Squid Game.

scenes.title_cn: 一、英伟达的赌注与边界（00:02:35）
scenes.context: 刘洺堉开篇定义英伟达的定位——运算公司而非 solution 公司，以及老黄「zero-billion-dollar business」的赌注哲学。语域：tech 高管访谈 + 商业哲学。
scenes.speak: Cosmos isn't aimed at the video-creation market — it's aimed at Physical AI, the next revolution in Ming-Yu's eyes, because it's a genuine need: people age and can't drive and their quality of life drops sharply; plenty of jobs are labor-intensive and dangerous; nobody wants to do the chores. These physical actors that can actually change the state of the physical world need world models. NVIDIA itself is a computing company, not a solutions company — its real strength is the whole computer stack. That comes with a difficulty: it's a bit like scratching an itch through your boot, because you don't know where the pain points are. That's why he comes to China two or three times a year. And Jensen loves the 'zero-billion-dollar business' — not a business today, but billion-scale if it succeeds. You can make no money now, but when it succeeds, it has to be hugely influential.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：Cosmos 瞄准的不是视频创作市场，而是 Physical AI——刘洺堉眼中的「下一个 revolution」，因为它是钢需：人年纪大了没法开车，生命品质会大幅下降；很多工作劳力密集又危险；家庭琐事没人想做。这些「真正能改变物理世界状态的 physical actor」需要世界模型来赋能
sentences.en: Cosmos isn't aimed at the video-creation market — it's aimed at Physical AI, the 'next revolution' in Ming-Yu's eyes, because it's a hard need: when you get old you can't drive and your quality of life drops sharply; many jobs are labor-intensive and dangerous; nobody wants to do household chores. These 'physical actors that can truly change the state of the physical world' need world models to empower them.
sentences.note: 表达提示Physical AI → 物理世界 AI；a hard need → 钢需；labor-intensive → 劳力密集；world model → 世界模型；quality of life → 生命品质

sentences.cn: 关键理解：英伟达是运算公司，不是 solution 公司——最厉害的是整个 computer stack（从底层芯片到软件），「我们并不是一个 solution 的公司，我们的目标是帮助这些建 solution 的公司成功」。这带来一个难处：「有点像隔靴搔痒，因为你不了解痛点在哪里」，所以他每年要来中国 2-3 次，就是为了理解开发者真正遇到的问题
sentences.en: NVIDIA is a computing company, not a solutions company — its real strength is the whole computer stack, from chips at the bottom to software. 'We're not a solutions company; our goal is to help the companies that build solutions succeed.' That brings one difficulty: 'it's a bit like scratching an itch through your boot, because you don't understand where the pain points are.' So he comes to China two or three times a year, just to understand the problems developers are actually facing.
sentences.note: 表达提示computing company vs solutions company → 运算公司与解决方案公司；computer stack → 从底层芯片到软件的整套技术栈；scratch an itch through your boot → 隔靴搔痒；pain point → 痛点

sentences.cn: 典型场景：判断一个研究/业务方向值不值得投入时——先问「这是不是够大的问题」，再问「它符不符合我这家公司的生态位置」
sentences.en: Typical use case: when judging whether a research or business direction deserves investment — first ask 'is this a big enough problem?', then ask 'does it fit my company's position in the ecosystem?'
sentences.note: 表达提示deserve investment → 值得投入；a big enough problem → 够大的问题；position in the ecosystem → 生态位置

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据（00:02:35）：「英伟达是一个运算公司……但我们并不是一个 solution 的公司，我们的目标是帮助这些建 solution 的公司成功。」
sentences.en: 'NVIDIA is a computing company … but we're not a solutions company; our goal is to help the companies that build solutions succeed.' (00:02:35)
sentences.note: 表达提示转述引用用现在时 is / are；solutions company → 解决方案公司；help … succeed → 帮助…成功

sentences.cn: （引用）与其他概念的关系：这是理解整场访谈的总纲——后续的 Cosmos、泛化、造市场都是在这个赌注之上展开
sentences.en: This is the master key to the whole interview — everything that follows, from Cosmos to generalization to building markets, unfolds on top of this bet.
sentences.note: 表达提示master key → 总纲；unfold on top of → 在…之上展开；generalization → 泛化；building markets → 造市场

sentences.cn: 在讲什么：老黄常讲他喜欢「zero-billion-dollar business」——现在还不是一个生意（zero），但成功后会是 billion 级别的生意。可以暂时不赚钱，但当它成功的时候必须很 influential、很巨大
sentences.en: Jensen often says he loves the 'zero-billion-dollar business' — it's not a business yet (zero), but if it succeeds it becomes a billion-dollar one. You can make no money for now, but when it succeeds it must be very influential and enormous.
sentences.note: 表达提示zero-billion-dollar business → 老黄造的词：现在零收入、成功后十亿级；billion-dollar → 十亿美金级别；influential → 有影响力的

paraphrase.intent: 想说「英伟达不直接做解决方案，而是赋能做解决方案的公司」
phrases: NVIDIA sells the picks and shovels, not the gold.
We don't build the solution — we power the people who do.
paraphrase.chunks: picks and shovels · power the people who do
paraphrase.usage: picks and shovels 是「卖铲子不挖金矿」的经典说法；第二句更口语直白

paraphrase.intent: 想说「现在不赚钱没关系，成功后要大」
phrases: Make no money today, change the world when it lands.
Zero revenue now, but if it works it's a billion-dollar market.
paraphrase.chunks: make no money today · when it lands
paraphrase.usage: 第一句口语化转述赌注；billion-dollar market 第二句更精确直白

scenes.context: 刘洺堉的成长轨迹：台北长大、赴美读博转计算机视觉、三菱电机三年、2016 年加入英伟达，以及两个关键转变。语域：career 自述 + 学习心态。
scenes.speak: Grew up in Taipei, studied wireless communication at National Chiao Tung University, decided in his junior year to go to the US — his parents were shocked — then a PhD at Maryland switching to computer vision, three years at Mitsubishi Electric Research, where the year he graduated AlexNet came out, and then NVIDIA in 2016, ten years and counting. AI was an accident for him: interning at Intel Taiwan, he saw systems that could identify objects from pixels and found it magical — because he didn't understand it, it was easy to see how important it was. When everything he'd learned in his PhD suddenly stopped working, he was fine, because 'learn everything' was already a habit. He even predicted in 2016 that language would break through first, but he liked visual signals more, so he stayed. The deeper turn was from the beauty of math to the essence of problems: assumptions make math cleaner but push you further from reality.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：台北长大 → 新竹交通大学学无线通讯 → 大三决定去美国（父母震惊）→ 马里兰大学读博转计算机视觉 → 三菱电机研究所三年（毕业那年 AlexNet 出现）→ 2016 年加入英伟达至今 10 年
sentences.en: Grew up in Taipei, studied wireless communication at National Chiao Tung University in Hsinchu, decided in his junior year to go to the US (his parents were shocked), did a PhD at the University of Maryland switching to computer vision, spent three years at Mitsubishi Electric Research — the year he graduated, AlexNet appeared — then joined NVIDIA in 2016, ten years and counting.
sentences.note: 表达提示junior year → 大三；switch to computer vision → 转计算机视觉；ten years and counting → 至今 10 年；AlexNet → 引爆深度学习的经典卷积网络

sentences.cn: 关键理解：AI 对他是一场意外。在台湾英特尔实习时第一次看到「从像素判断物件」的语音/图像识别，觉得神奇；「因为不懂，所以很容易理解它的重要性」。博士期间学的 SVM、图形模型在他毕业那年突然「什么都不 work」了，但他早已养成「什么都学」的习惯。他 2016-2017 年就预判「真正产生突破的第一个领域是 language」，只是「比较喜欢视觉信号，所以一直留在这里」
sentences.en: AI was an accident for him. Interning at Intel Taiwan, he saw speech and image recognition that could 'judge objects from pixels' for the first time and found it magical — 'because I didn't understand it, it was easy to understand its importance.' The SVM and graphical models he learned in his PhD suddenly 'stopped working' the year he graduated, but he'd long built the habit of 'learning everything.' As early as 2016-2017 he predicted that 'the first field to truly break through is language,' only 'he likes visual signals more, so he's stayed here.'
sentences.note: 表达提示SVM（support vector machine）→ 支持向量机；graphical model → 图形模型；break through → 产生突破；visual signal → 视觉信号；judge objects from pixels → 从像素判断物件

sentences.cn: 典型场景：当一条路走到头、时代切换时，怎么不慌——把「学过的都不 work」看成常态，把「什么都学」养成习惯
sentences.en: Typical scenario: when a path dead-ends and the era shifts, how not to panic — treat 'everything I learned stopped working' as the norm, and make 'learning everything' a habit.
sentences.note: 表达提示dead-end → 走到头；era shift → 时代切换；treat sth as the norm → 把…看成常态；make sth a habit → 养成…的习惯

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据（00:29:57）：大三那年告诉父母要去美国留学，「他们吓了一跳，因为认识我 20 几年，没有听过我讲说我要去美国留学这件事情」
sentences.en: In his junior year he told his parents he was going to study in the US: 'they were startled, because they'd known me for over 20 years and never once heard me mention going to the US to study.' (00:29:57)
sentences.note: 表达提示be startled → 吓了一跳；never once → 一次也没有；mention doing sth → 提到要做某事

sentences.cn: （引用）与其他概念的关系：这条轨迹解释了为什么他会成为英伟达第一个「把生成式网络带起来」的研究员——不是规划出来的，是走一步看一步走出来的
sentences.en: This trajectory explains why he became NVIDIA's first researcher to 'bring generative networks up' — it wasn't planned out; it was built one step at a time.
sentences.note: 表达提示trajectory → 轨迹；generative network → 生成式网络；one step at a time → 走一步看一步

sentences.cn: 时刻一 · 从数学的美到问题的本质：早期做优化，为了证明 bound 会做很多假设，「假设让你的数学变得比较干净，但也让你离现实比较远」。后来认识到 AI 本身就是应用，「越来越喜欢接近问题的本质，而不会被花巧的数学迷惑」
sentences.en: Turn one: from the beauty of math to the essence of the problem. Early on, to prove bounds he'd make lots of assumptions — 'assumptions make your math cleaner, but they also push you further from reality.' Later he realized AI is itself an application, and he 'increasingly liked getting close to the essence of problems, without being seduced by fancy math.'
sentences.note: 表达提示prove a bound → 证明界（数学术语）；make assumptions → 做假设；the essence of the problem → 问题的本质；fancy math → 花巧的数学；be seduced by → 被…迷惑

paraphrase.intent: 想说「时代切换时别慌」
phrases: When the field shifts under you, treating it as normal beats panicking.
If your old toolbox stops working, that's a signal to learn, not to panic.
paraphrase.chunks: shifts under you · old toolbox stops working
paraphrase.usage: 第一句偏正式总结；第二句用 toolbox 比喻，口语更形象

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不要被炫技的数学迷惑」
phrases: Don't let elegant math distract you from the real problem.
Fancy math is seductive, but reality is the boss.
paraphrase.chunks: elegant math · reality is the boss
paraphrase.usage: reality is the boss 呼应访谈的「以问题为本」态度，口语有力

scenes.title_cn: 三、如何在英伟达拿到 GPU（01:02:46）
scenes.title_en: How to Win GPUs at NVIDIA
scenes.context: 聊研究如何争取算力：懂公司要解的问题、解释影响、对齐兴趣与公司利益，并用 DALL·E 后拿到 1000 张 A100 的故事佐证。语域：职场生存 + 内部决策故事。
scenes.speak: On winning GPUs: there's no place on earth where GPUs are enough, so you have to understand the problem the company is solving and explain why your work will have an impact on the company. Researchers tend to have high egos and look down on each other, but a company exists to profit its shareholders — Jensen wants to take care of the family. He saw it firsthand at Mitsubishi Electric Research: once a peer of Microsoft Research in the nineties, until the company doubted blue-sky research and a bunch of important scholars got fired. So he aligns his interest with the company's. When DALL·E came out, he wrote to Jensen: the future is already clear — image generation will run on deep learning, we must invest in GPUs. He got 1,000 A100s, a lot in the Ampere era. And he doesn't get excited about temporary model leads, because this month GPT is better, next month Anthropic, the month after open source catches up, and China's GLM, Kimi, Alibaba, DeepSeek, MiniMax keep pushing — eventually everyone's models converge.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：「你要懂公司要解的问题是什么，然后你要想办法跟公司解释，为什么你做的东西会对公司产生影响。」研究员普遍 high ego、文人相轻，但公司的本质是为股东获利——老黄希望 take care of family，公司要赚钱
sentences.en: 'You have to understand the problem the company is trying to solve, then find a way to explain to the company why what you're doing will have an impact on it.' Researchers generally have high egos and look down on each other, but a company exists to make a profit for its shareholders — Jensen wants to take care of the family, and the company has to make money.
sentences.note: 表达提示high ego → 自我很强；look down on each other → 文人相轻；take care of the family → 照顾家人（老黄常用语）；have an impact on → 对…产生影响

sentences.cn: 关键理解：他亲眼见过三菱电机研究院的教训：90 年代它是和微软研究院并驾齐驱的机构，但当公司方向改变、开始怀疑 blue sky research 的价值时，「一堆重要的学者陆陆续续被 fired」。所以做研究「要让自己的兴趣跟公司的兴趣可以对齐」，尤其在 deep learning 这种极其烧钱的领域，更要解释「为什么这对公司是一个重要的投资」
sentences.en: He witnessed the lesson at Mitsubishi Electric Research firsthand: in the nineties it was an institution on par with Microsoft Research, but when the company changed direction and started doubting the value of blue-sky research, 'a bunch of important scholars got fired one after another.' So when doing research, 'you need to align your interest with the company's interest' — especially in a money-burning field like deep learning, you need to explain 'why this is an important investment for the company.'
sentences.note: 表达提示on par with → 与…并驾齐驱；blue-sky research → 蓝天/基础研究；get fired one after another → 陆陆续续被解雇；align A with B → 让 A 与 B 对齐；money-burning → 极其烧钱的

sentences.cn: 怎么用：每次立项先回答「这对公司为什么重要、和我们的生意有什么关系」——这不是妥协，是生存技能
sentences.en: How to use it: before every project, answer first 'why does this matter to the company, and how does it relate to our business?' — that's not compromise, it's a survival skill.
sentences.note: 表达提示survival skill → 生存技能；not compromise → 不是妥协；matter to the company → 对公司重要

sentences.cn: （引用）「这世界上没有任何一个地方 GPU 是够的。」
sentences.en: 'There is no place on this earth where GPUs are enough.'
sentences.note: 表达提示GPU → 图形处理器（此指算力芯片）；enough → 够用；引用时注意用引号括起原话

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据（01:02:46）：DALL·E 出来之后他写信给老黄：「这个未来已经很明确了，就是靠 deep learning 来做影像生成……我们必须投资 GPU。」最终拿到 1000 张 A100——在当时（Ampere 时代）「非常的多」
sentences.en: After DALL·E came out, he wrote to Jensen: 'the future is already clear — it's deep learning doing image generation … we must invest in GPUs.' He ended up getting 1,000 A100s — 'a whole lot' for the Ampere era at the time. (01:02:46)
sentences.note: 表达提示DALL·E → OpenAI 图像生成模型；A100 → 英伟达旗舰数据中心 GPU；Ampere era → Ampere 架构时代；a whole lot → 非常多

sentences.cn: 在讲什么：为什么不为模型暂时的领先而兴奋？因为「这个月 GPT 比较好，下个月 Anthropic 比较好，可能下下个月开源模型就追上来了，然后中国这些强大的公司——GLM、Kimi、阿里、DeepSeek、MiniMax——都在不断突破，慢慢大家的模型能力都会差不多」
sentences.en: Why doesn't he get excited about a model's temporary lead? Because 'this month GPT is better, next month Anthropic is better, the month after open-source models may catch up, and China's strong players — GLM, Kimi, Alibaba, DeepSeek, MiniMax — keep breaking through, so slowly everyone's model capability ends up about the same.'
sentences.note: 表达提示temporary lead → 暂时的领先；open-source model → 开源模型；catch up → 追上；break through → 不断突破；converge → 趋同

paraphrase.intent: 想说「研究要与公司利益对齐」
phrases: Your research has to speak the company's language.
Align your curiosity with the company's business, or it dies in the lab.
paraphrase.chunks: speak the company's language · align your curiosity
paraphrase.usage: speak the language 是比喻「说同一套话」；第二句点出利害关系，更口语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「模型能力终将趋同」
phrases: Model quality is converging — leads are temporary.
Everyone will end up in the same ballpark on model ability.
paraphrase.chunks: converging · in the same ballpark
paraphrase.usage: in the same ballpark 是非常地道的口语，指水平接近

scenes.title_cn: 四、从研究员到英伟达 VP（01:21:57）
scenes.context: 聊晋升路径、带 Cosmos 团队的信任基础，以及「别跟底层脱钩」的管理自省。语域：career 复盘 + 管理心得。
scenes.speak: 'I might be the first one, yeah' — researcher straight up to VP, a level a year in the early years. He helped NVIDIA build AI research credibility before it had AI talent, he genuinely loves shipping — turning research into products — and he earned trust step by step. Now the Cosmos team burns millions of dollars of compute a day, and that trust is exactly why he gets to lead a project this big. His biggest worry as a manager is losing touch with the fundamentals, so he stays one of the few VPs who still reads code — he reviews code, reads papers, and challenges every idea. The Cosmos paper has over 290 authors, and managing that is a tug between total alignment and individual autonomy: too aligned and you get horse-racing, too centralized and progress crawls.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：「我可能是第一个（从研究员做到 VP）吧。」前几年每年升一级，一直跳到 VP。原因有三：早期英伟达还没有 AI 人才时，他帮助公司提升 AI 研究知名度、解释 AI 怎么影响公司；自己又很喜欢落地（research 变成产品）；一步一步获得公司信任，公司就愿意把越来越大规模的项目交给他
sentences.en: 'I might be the first one, yeah.' In the first few years he was promoted a level every year, all the way to VP. Three reasons: early on, when NVIDIA had no AI talent yet, he helped raise the company's AI research profile and explained how AI would affect it; he also genuinely loved shipping — turning research into products; and he earned the company's trust step by step, so it kept handing him bigger and bigger projects.
sentences.note: 表达提示be promoted a level every year → 每年升一级；raise the profile → 提升知名度；shipping → 落地、把东西做出来；earn trust step by step → 一步步获得信任

sentences.cn: 关键理解：现在整个 Cosmos 团队每天烧掉几百万美金的运算成本——「公司有一定的信任，才有这个机会去带这么大的 project。所以你跟公司 align 非常重要。」
sentences.en: The whole Cosmos team now burns millions of dollars of compute every day — 'the company only gives you this chance to lead a project this big if it has a certain level of trust in you. So aligning with the company is very important.'
sentences.note: 表达提示burn millions of dollars → 烧掉几百万美金；compute cost → 算力成本；align with the company → 与公司对齐

sentences.cn: 风险警示：他成为管理者后最担心的一件事是「跟底层脱钩」——所以至今仍是「少数还在看 code 的 VP」，会继续 review 大家的代码、读 paper、challenge 每个人的 idea
sentences.en: The risk warning: the thing he worries about most as a manager is 'losing touch with the fundamentals' — that's why he's still 'one of the few VPs who still read code', keeping on reviewing everyone's code, reading papers, and challenging each person's idea.
sentences.note: 表达提示lose touch with → 与…脱钩；read code → 看代码；challenge an idea → 质疑某个想法；the fundamentals → 底层/基本面

sentences.cn: （引用）「我最担心的是我跟底层脱钩，我不理解问题的核心所在。我会强迫自己 review 大家的 code，去读 paper，去 challenge 每个人的 idea。」
sentences.en: 'What I worry about most is losing touch with the fundamentals and not understanding the core of the problem. I force myself to review everyone's code, read papers, and challenge each person's idea.'
sentences.note: 表达提示the core of the problem → 问题的核心所在；force oneself to do → 强迫自己做

sentences.cn: （引用）落地建议：管理者的自我保鲜——保留一个「动手回路」：哪怕不做实现，也要定期读代码、读论文、参与技术辩论，保持对问题本质的触觉
sentences.en: Actionable takeaway: a manager's self-freshness plan — keep a 'hands-on loop': even if you don't implement, read code and papers regularly and join technical debates, keeping your feel for the essence of problems.
sentences.note: 表达提示hands-on loop → 动手回路；keep one's feel for → 保持对…的触觉；technical debate → 技术辩论

sentences.cn: 在讲什么：Cosmos 论文署名 290 多人、不到 300 人。管理一个这么大的团队的难点是两条线的张力：目标一致（否则发散、出现赛马行为）与人人可自主决策（否则只有少数决策者，进展缓慢）
sentences.en: The Cosmos paper lists over 290 authors — just under 300. Managing a team that big is a tug between two lines: everyone aligned on the goal (or it diverges and you get horse-racing behavior) and everyone able to decide on their own (or only a few decide and progress crawls).
sentences.note: 表达提示paper authorship → 论文署名；a tug between A and B → A 与 B 之间的张力；horse-racing → 赛马行为；progress crawls → 进展缓慢

paraphrase.intent: 想说「管理者不能脱离一线」
phrases: Once you go all-management, you go blind.
Managers who stop reading code lose their grip on the problem.
paraphrase.chunks: go blind · lose their grip on
paraphrase.usage: go all-management 押韵、口语感强；lose their grip 偏正式

paraphrase.intent: 想说「信任换来大项目」
phrases: Big projects go to people the company trusts.
Trust is the currency that buys you the big bets.
paraphrase.chunks: trust is the currency · the big bets
paraphrase.usage: trust is the currency 很凝练，适合做金句；big bets 指大项目大押注

scenes.context: Cosmos 的起源：10 年前的 Job Talk、DALL·E 的刺激、Sora 后的立项，以及为什么从视频生成做进物理世界。语域：产品起源故事 + 决策复盘。
scenes.speak: Ten years ago, in his job talk at NVIDIA, he said the day would come when video generation ran on deep neural networks instead of traditional computer graphics. He built GANs and GauGAN — named after the painter Gauguin — and the Deep Imagination Research Group. When DALL·E appeared, he realized his ambition, courage, and resolve weren't big enough: the conditions were all there; he just didn't go do it. After Sora, he and his team wrote to Jensen — we have to do this — and Cosmos was born in March 2024. Jensen's reply: just go to Cosmos 97. Now at Cosmos 3, with 94 generations to go. His direct team is under a hundred, with a few hundred more reporting in loosely. And why video, not language? Computer-vision background, a great LLM team at NVIDIA already, and Physical AI needs actors that change the physical world.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：10 年前加入英伟达的 Job Talk 他就说：「有一天最主要生成视频的运算将会是 deep neural（深度神经网络），而不会是传统的 computer graphics。」之后在英伟达做了 GAN、GauGAN（取名自画家高更）、StyleGAN 团队合作，建立 Deep Imagination Research Group，又做了 Picasso（AI foundry，与 Getty Images、Shutterstock 合作）
sentences.en: Ten years ago, in his job talk before joining NVIDIA, he said: 'one day the main compute for generating video will be deep neural networks, not traditional computer graphics.' After that, at NVIDIA he worked on GANs and GauGAN — named after the painter Gauguin — collaborated with the StyleGAN team, founded the Deep Imagination Research Group, and built Picasso, an AI foundry in partnership with Getty Images and Shutterstock.
sentences.note: 表达提示job talk → 求职报告；deep neural network → 深度神经网络；computer graphics → 传统计算机图形学；GAN → 生成对抗网络；AI foundry → 模型代工厂；in partnership with → 与…合作

sentences.cn: 关键理解：DALL·E 出现让他意识到「我的野心不够大、不够勇敢、没有决心」——条件其实已经具备，「只是因为没有去做，所以做不出来」。Sora 出来后，他带着团队写信给老黄「我们必须做这个」，这就是 Cosmos 的由来（2024 年 3 月立项，就在 Sora 之后）。老黄回应的方式是一句话：「你就做到 Cosmos 97」——他随口说出的数字，展现的是对这个方向的决心
sentences.en: When DALL·E appeared, he realized 'my ambition wasn't big enough, I wasn't brave enough, I didn't have the resolve' — the conditions were actually all there; 'it's just because I didn't do it, so it didn't get made.' After Sora came out, he led the team to write to Jensen 'we must do this' — that's how Cosmos came to be (kicked off in March 2024, right after Sora). Jensen's reply was one line: 'just make it to Cosmos 97' — an offhand number that showed his resolve on this direction.
sentences.note: 表达提示ambition → 野心；resolve → 决心；kick off → 立项；offhand → 随口说出的；Sora → OpenAI 视频生成模型

sentences.cn: 怎么用：看到一个比你想象的更大的突破时，不是懊悔「我没想到」，而是问「我缺的是能力还是决心」——刘的答案是两者都有，但决心缺口更大
sentences.en: How to use it: when you see a breakthrough bigger than you imagined, don't just regret 'I didn't think of it' — ask 'did I lack ability or resolve?' Liu's answer: both, but the resolve gap was bigger.
sentences.note: 表达提示breakthrough → 突破；regret → 懊悔；lack ability / resolve → 缺能力/决心；the gap → 缺口

sentences.cn: （引用）「我们就做完 Cosmos 1 的时候问老黄要不要继续往下做，老黄跟我说：你就做到 Cosmos 97。我现在做到 3 而已，还有 94 代可以往下走。」
sentences.en: 'When we finished Cosmos 1, we asked Jensen whether to keep going, and he told me: just make it to Cosmos 97. I'm only at 3 now, so there are still 94 generations to go.'
sentences.note: 表达提示keep going → 继续往下做；only at … → 才做到…；generations to go → 还有多少代可以往下走

sentences.cn: （引用）团队规模（01:37:00）：直属团队不到 100 人（研究员 + 工程师），虚线汇报 200-300 人；项目从 research 独立出来，改名 Cosmos Lab
sentences.en: Team size (01:37:00): his direct team is under 100 people (researchers plus engineers), with 200-300 reporting in loosely; the project split off from research and renamed itself Cosmos Lab.
sentences.note: 表达提示direct team → 直属团队；report in loosely / dotted-line → 虚线汇报；split off from → 从…独立出来

sentences.cn: 核心机制：三个原因：① 背景是 computer vision 而不是 NLP，跟着他的伙伴也是类似背景，「更想解一些更适合我来解的问题」；② 英伟达已经有强大的大语言模型团队（Nemotron），「我觉得我没有太多的贡献，Nemotron 越做越好」；③ 看到 physical AI 发展极快、同时很多问题需要「真正能改变物理世界状态的 physical actor」来解
sentences.en: Three reasons: ① his background is computer vision rather than NLP, and the partners who follow him have similar backgrounds — 'we'd rather solve problems that fit me better'; ② NVIDIA already has a strong LLM team (Nemotron), and 'I don't feel I have much to contribute — Nemotron is getting better and better on its own'; ③ he sees Physical AI developing extremely fast, with many problems that need 'physical actors that can truly change the state of the physical world' to solve them.
sentences.note: 表达提示LLM（large language model）→ 大语言模型；NLP → 自然语言处理；contribute → 作出贡献；fit sb → 适合某人

paraphrase.intent: 想说「缺的不是能力，是决心」
phrases: It wasn't capability I lacked — it was nerve.
The gap wasn't skill; it was the courage to commit.
paraphrase.chunks: lacked nerve · the courage to commit
paraphrase.usage: nerve 比 courage 更口语；commit 表达押上去的决心

paraphrase.intent: 想说「老大一句话就定调了」
phrases: One number from Jensen set the whole direction.
Jensen's offhand 'go to 97' was the green light.
paraphrase.chunks: set the whole direction · the green light
paraphrase.usage: green light 是很常用的「放行」说法；set the whole direction 更正式

scenes.context: 为什么从 22 个模型收敛到一个 Omni 模型，以及「备多则力寡」的产品第一性原理。语域：技术决策 + 产品哲学。
scenes.speak: For Cosmos 1, he counted up what partners needed and landed on about 22 models. In the meeting, Jensen answered with what sounded like an unrelated story: Louis Vuitton cut its displays and sales went up — too many options confuse customers and stop them from deciding. Twenty-two models would each need maintenance and support; soldiers scattered in too many places is weak, and it slows iteration. So Cosmos 1 to 2 was just better data, but 2 to 3 was a leap: folding Reason, Predict, Transfer, Parser into a single Omni model, because no matter which path you take, you're modeling the same internal representation of the world, and a foundation model is meant to absorb everything. When a founder said Cosmos 3 isn't full of innovation but engineering-validates the details, Liu replied: the details are exactly what makes some models much better than others. He cares more about the effect than revolutionary originality.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：做 Cosmos 1 时，他算了算 partner 的需求，「可能需要 22 个模型」，于是开会跟老黄汇报。老黄回了一个看似不相关的例子：LV（Louis Vuitton）减少货品陈列后，销售反而提升——「你不希望太多的东西困惑你的消费者，让他没办法做出决定」
sentences.en: When building Cosmos 1, he counted up what partners needed — 'probably 22 models' — and reported it to Jensen in a meeting. Jensen answered with what looked like an unrelated example: when LV (Louis Vuitton) reduced its product displays, sales actually went up — 'you don't want too many things confusing your consumers and stopping them from making a decision.'
sentences.note: 表达提示count up → 算了算；product display → 货品陈列；sales went up → 销售提升；confuse your consumers → 困惑你的消费者

sentences.cn: 关键理解：模型多了，每个都要维护、都要帮用户用，「很辛苦，备多则力寡，而且影响你迭代的速度」。所以 Cosmos 1→2 只是数据提升，而 2→3 是巨大跨越：把 Reason/Predict/Transfer/Parser 等全部收敛为一个 Omni 模型（multimodal transformer，把 audio、video、action 都合在一起）——因为「无论你从哪条路看，model 的都是同一个世界的 internal representation」，而且 foundation model 的本质就是「纳百川」、吸收各式各样的数据
sentences.en: Too many models means each one needs maintenance and user support — 'it's exhausting; too many soldiers scatter your strength (备多则力寡), and it slows your iteration.' So Cosmos 1→2 was just a data upgrade, while 2→3 was a huge leap: folding Reason, Predict, Transfer, Parser and the rest into a single Omni model — a multimodal transformer that brings audio, video, and action together — because 'no matter which path you look from, what's modeled is the same internal representation of the world,' and the essence of a foundation model is to 'take in all streams' (纳百川), absorbing all kinds of data.
sentences.note: 表达提示备多则力寡 → too many soldiers scatter your strength（孙子兵法）；iteration speed → 迭代速度；Omni model → 单一全能模型；multimodal transformer → 多模态 Transformer；internal representation → 内部表征；纳百川 → take in all streams

sentences.cn: 怎么用：产品线管理的第一性原理——每多一个 SKU/模型，就多一份维护与决策成本；用户分不清 A 还是 B，产品自己也会被拖垮
sentences.en: How to use it: the first principle of product-line management — every extra SKU or model adds a piece of maintenance and decision cost; if users can't tell A from B, the product drags itself down.
sentences.note: 表达提示first principle → 第一性原理；maintenance cost → 维护成本；can't tell A from B → 分不清 A 还是 B；drag sth down → 拖垮

sentences.cn: （引用）「备多则力寡（孙子兵法）——大家的资源都是有限的。」
sentences.en: 'Too many soldiers scatter your strength (Sun Tzu) — everyone's resources are limited.'
sentences.note: 表达提示Sun Tzu → 孙子；scatter one's strength → 力寡；resources are limited → 资源有限

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据（01:51:39）：中国一位做世界模型的创业者评价 Cosmos 3「技术创新不多，但把很多细节都工程验证出来了」。刘的回答：「所有的大语言模型都是 transformer 架构，你可以讲大家都没有创新，但是那些细节会让某些模型比另外一些模型好很多。我越来越重视这东西能产生的效果，越来越不重视它是不是革命性的原创。」
sentences.en: A Chinese founder building world models commented that Cosmos 3 'doesn't have much technical innovation, but it engineering-validated a lot of details.' Liu's reply: 'all the big language models are transformer-based, so you could say nobody's innovating — but those details make some models much better than others. I increasingly value the effect it can produce, and increasingly don't care whether it's a revolutionary original.' (01:51:39)
sentences.note: 表达提示engineering-validate → 工程验证；revolutionary original → 革命性的原创；value the effect → 重视效果

sentences.cn: 核心机制：Cosmos 3 采用双塔：一个塔处理离散信号（understanding/reason，从 Vision-Language Model 出发），一个塔处理连续信号（generation，diffusion 路径）。「我们知道离散的 work for understanding，连续的 work for generation。」
sentences.en: Cosmos 3 uses a two-tower design: one tower handles discrete signals (understanding and reasoning, built from a Vision-Language Model), the other handles continuous signals (generation, via the diffusion path). 'We know discrete works for understanding, and continuous works for generation.'
sentences.note: 表达提示discrete vs continuous signal → 离散与连续信号；vision-language model → 视觉语言模型；diffusion path → 扩散路径；work for … → 适用于…

paraphrase.intent: 想说「产品线越多越拖累」
phrases: Every extra model is a tax on your team.
More SKUs, more drag — the catalog chokes itself.
paraphrase.chunks: a tax on your team · more drag
paraphrase.usage: tax 比喻隐性维护成本；chokes itself 有画面感，很口语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「细节决定模型好坏」
phrases: The gap is in the details, not the architecture.
What separates good models from great ones is engineering, not novelty.
paraphrase.chunks: the gap is in the details · engineering, not novelty
paraphrase.usage: 两句都是总结观点句；第一句更简洁，第二句更完整

scenes.title_en: 'The Matrix': Robots and the World Model
scenes.context: 刘洺堉的个人愿景「为机器人构建一个黑客帝国」，泛化的定义，以及 AI 会不会 take over the world 的哲学讨论。语域：vision 陈述 + 哲学对谈。
scenes.speak: His vision statement on his homepage: build a Matrix for robots — a concrete way to think about what world models do. Generalization is the problem every AI must solve: can you perform well beyond your training data? For Physical AI, the hardest generalization is learning the needed operations from limited signals and applying them in a scene you've never seen — observation and action working together. The host pushes: The Matrix is about humans becoming living batteries and the awakened breaking free — what if robots awaken one day and want to break out of the virtual world? His answer has three layers. First, the world is built by people and tech is operated by people; with shared consensus it won't happen. Second, deeper: thinking and suffering drive human progress, and he's genuinely not sure silicon-made intelligence has the same thinking and suffering. Third, we need guardrails. He leaves the question open.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：他的个人主页愿景是「为机器人构建一个黑客帝国」，帮大家具象理解世界模型的作用。世界模型帮助 physical AI 泛化的三个抓手：
sentences.en: His personal-homepage vision is 'building a Matrix for robots', to help people concretely understand what world models do. The world model helps Physical AI generalize through three handles:
sentences.note: 表达提示vision → 愿景；make sth concrete → 具象化理解；handle → 抓手；generalize → 泛化

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「任何 AI 要解的问题，就是泛化的问题——你能不能在你看过的训练数据之外，也表现得非常好。」physical AI 最难的泛化是「从有限的讯号里面学到需要的操作，然后应用在一个没有看过的场景里面」——这是 observation 与 action 配合的泛化
sentences.en: 'The problem any AI has to solve is generalization — can you perform very well beyond the training data you've seen?' The hardest generalization for Physical AI is 'learning the needed operations from limited signals, then applying them in a scene you've never seen' — generalization where observation and action work together.
sentences.note: 表达提示generalization → 泛化；beyond the training data → 训练数据之外；limited signals → 有限的讯号；unseen scene → 没看过的场景

sentences.cn: （引用）「大多数人都担心 AI 能力太强会 take over the world……但这个世界是人去建立的，这些科技是人在背后操作的。只要大家有共识，我觉得这件事情不会发生。」
sentences.en: 'Most people worry that AI being too capable will take over the world … but this world is built by people, and these technologies are operated by people behind the scenes. As long as there's shared consensus, I don't think it will happen.'
sentences.note: 表达提示take over the world → 接管世界；behind the scenes → 在背后；shared consensus → 共识

sentences.cn: 主持人提问：《黑客帝国》讲的正是人类沦为机器的活体电池、觉醒者挣脱虚拟系统——如果有一天机器人觉醒了想挣脱这个虚拟世界怎么办？
sentences.en: The host's question: The Matrix is exactly about humans becoming the machines' living batteries and the awakened ones breaking free of the virtual system — what if one day robots awaken and want to break out of this virtual world?
sentences.note: 表达提示living battery → 活体电池；the awakened → 觉醒者；break free of → 挣脱；break out of → 逃出

sentences.cn: 嘉宾回应（三层）：① 社会是人建立的，科技由人操作，只要人有共识，不会发生；② 更深一层，「Thinking and Suffering（思考与痛苦）是驱动人去进步的一个重要关键——我不确定这些 silicon 做成的 intelligence 是不是有同样的 thinking and suffering」，他心里存疑；③ 需要相应的 guardrail 确保它不会影响正常世界的发展
sentences.en: His three-layer response: ① society is built by people and tech is operated by people, so with consensus it won't happen; ② deeper still — 'thinking and suffering are a key driver of human progress — I'm not sure intelligence made of silicon has the same thinking and suffering,' and he genuinely has doubts; ③ we need appropriate guardrails to make sure it doesn't affect the development of the normal world.
sentences.note: 表达提示thinking and suffering → 思考与痛苦（进步驱动力）；silicon-made intelligence → 硅基智能；guardrail → 护栏/安全机制；have doubts → 心里存疑

sentences.cn: 争议保留：这是一段开放性的哲学讨论，他没有给出确定答案，而是把问题留在「不确定硅基智能是否有同样的痛苦驱动力」上——这恰好呼应他「把模型当中医」的经验主义立场
sentences.en: Open question left open: this is an open-ended philosophical discussion — he doesn't give a firm answer, leaving the question at 'not sure silicon intelligence has the same suffering-driven motivation,' which exactly echoes his empiricist stance of 'treating models like traditional Chinese medicine.'
sentences.note: 表达提示open-ended → 开放性的；leave the question open → 保留争议；empiricist stance → 经验主义立场；traditional Chinese medicine → 中医（比喻经验驱动）

paraphrase.intent: 想说「AI 是否接管世界取决于人」
phrases: Machines won't take over — people run the show.
The takeover question is really a question about consensus.
paraphrase.chunks: run the show · the takeover question
paraphrase.usage: run the show 是地道口语「做主」；第二句把问题重新定义，更有思辨感

paraphrase.intent: 想说「硅基智能也许没有痛苦驱动力」
phrases: Silicon may think, but does it suffer?
Without suffering, does silicon have the drive to evolve?
paraphrase.chunks: does it suffer · the drive to evolve
paraphrase.usage: 短问句更有力度，适合口头哲学讨论；第二句更书面

scenes.context: 未来软件以 AI 为核心、Nemotron/Cosmos 是否会是下一个 CUDA，以及复制 CUDA 的方法论。语域：战略推演 + 技术历史。
scenes.speak: In the past, software was about building logic, and CUDA helped convert the logic that applications needed into GPU computation. Future software is AI-centric — AI on top of other AI. So in his view, both Nemotron and Cosmos could be the next CUDA, because there's a huge ecosystem of services and tooling hanging off CUDA. But he won't draw an equals sign: the industry is far more complex now; many different stacks combine, and the combination may be the new CUDA, not any single model. CUDA succeeded because from day one it hunted for applications — scientific computing first, then deep learning as the killer app. Copying CUDA is a great idea, but the environment is different; you have to adapt and see clearly which important contributions you can make at which point in time. Jensen won't go hunting for nails with a hammer — he's a first-principles person.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：「过去的软件是建立逻辑，CUDA 是帮助把这些 application 所需要的逻辑转换成 GPU 的运算；未来的软件是以 AI 为核心的，AI 是 be on top of other AI。」所以在他看来，做 Nemotron 与 Cosmos 都可能是未来的 CUDA——因为外部对 CUDA 有非常多的附盘（服务、生态）
sentences.en: 'In the past, software was about building logic; CUDA helped convert the logic those applications needed into GPU computation. Future software is AI-centric — AI on top of other AI.' So in his view, doing Nemotron and Cosmos could both be the future CUDA — because there's a huge ecosystem of services and support hanging off CUDA.
sentences.note: 表达提示AI on top of other AI → AI 层层叠叠、互为底座；hanging off … → 附在…之上；ecosystem of services → 服务生态

sentences.cn: 关键理解：但他不会把 Cosmos 或 Nemotron 与 CUDA 划等号——「现在的产业发展已经复杂很多，有很多个不同的 stack 合在一起，合在一起可能是新的 CUDA，而不会说这个模型单一就是一个 CUDA。」CUDA 成功的要素是「一开始就在寻找 application——先是 scientific computing，deep learning 出来后找到最重要的 application」；复制 CUDA 是很好的想法，但「环境不一样，要 adaptive，要看清楚在哪个时间点可以做出哪些重要的贡献」
sentences.en: But he won't draw an equals sign between Cosmos or Nemotron and CUDA — 'the industry today has gotten far more complex; many different stacks come together, and the combination may be the new CUDA, rather than any single model being a CUDA.' The key to CUDA's success: 'from the very start it kept looking for applications — first scientific computing, then when deep learning came along it found the most important application.' Copying CUDA is a great idea, but 'the environment is different; you have to be adaptive and see clearly which important contributions you can make at which point in time.'
sentences.note: 表达提示draw an equals sign between → 把…划等号；stack → 技术栈；scientific computing → 科学计算；be adaptive → 因地制宜、随环境调整

sentences.cn: （引用）「不会拿着这个锤子去找钉子。老黄是非常 first principle 的人，他觉得什么合理，就往那个方向走。」
sentences.en: 'He won't take this hammer and go looking for nails. Jensen is a very first-principles person — whatever he feels is reasonable, he goes in that direction.'
sentences.note: 表达提示go looking for nails with a hammer → 拿着锤子找钉子；first-principles → 第一性原理

sentences.cn: （引用）与其他概念的关系：这是「造市场」哲学的技术推演——下一个 CUDA 不是另一个「编译器」，而是让 AI 生态在英伟达底座上长出来的整套东西
sentences.en: This is the technical extension of the 'building markets' philosophy — the next CUDA isn't another 'compiler'; it's the whole set of things that lets the AI ecosystem grow on NVIDIA's foundation.
sentences.note: 表达提示technical extension → 技术推演；building markets → 造市场；compiler → 编译器；grow on the foundation → 在底座上长出来

paraphrase.intent: 想说「下一个 CUDA 可能是组合，不是单品」
phrases: The next CUDA won't be a single product — it'll be a stack.
CUDA 2.0 is probably a combination of many stacks.
paraphrase.chunks: a combination of many stacks · CUDA 2.0
paraphrase.usage: CUDA 2.0 是通俗叫法；stack 是行话，两句分别适合口语与书面

paraphrase.intent: 想说「先找应用再做平台」
phrases: Find the application first; the platform will follow.
CUDA won because it chased the killer app, not the other way around.
paraphrase.chunks: the platform will follow · the other way around
paraphrase.usage: 第二句有因果感，适合做总结；killer app 指杀手级应用

scenes.title_cn: 九、关于黄仁勋：Mission is the boss（02:47:04）
scenes.title_en: Jensen Huang: Mission Is the Boss
scenes.context: 老黄的管理哲学：任务导向、Top 5 邮件、不裁员文化，以及这种文化的红利与代价。语域：组织文化观察 + 内部视角。
scenes.speak: Jensen's management keyword: mission is the boss — not your boss. The company works like an organism, not a fixed org chart: when the company moves in a direction, the relevant skills across groups align by themselves, and it doesn't matter where you sit. Cosmos is a case in point — lots of people outside the team came to support it. The Top 5 email backs that up: every employee writes their five most important things each week, visible company-wide, so the big and small signals are clear — if two teams are doing the same thing, reading the Top 5s makes it pop right out. Jensen reads a massive amount of email and makes decisions fast, every day. NVIDIA also never lays people off, and there's no stack-ranking — only performance reviews. The upside is straight talk and real collaboration; the cost is that transitions take longer than hiring people who already know. During the pandemic, when others were firing, NVIDIA cut travel and even considered dropping Slack.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：老黄的管理关键词：Mission is the boss（任务才是老板，而不是你的老板）。公司像有机体而不是固定框架——当公司要走向某个方向时，不同组织的相关技能会自发对齐，「你在这个公司哪里都没关系，但你往这个方向前进的时候，你的团队的智慧产生的贡献全部都能 align」。Cosmos 就是这样一个案例：很多人不属于这个团队，但都来支持它
sentences.en: Jensen's management keyword: 'mission is the boss' — the mission, not your boss. The company works like an organism rather than a fixed framework — when the company wants to move in a direction, the relevant skills in different organizations align by themselves. 'It doesn't matter where you are in this company — when you advance in that direction, all the contributions produced by your team's intelligence can align.' Cosmos is exactly such a case: many people don't belong to the team, but all came to support it.
sentences.note: 表达提示mission is the boss → 任务才是老板；organism → 有机体；align by themselves → 自发对齐；a case in point → 恰好的例子

sentences.cn: 支撑机制 · Top 5 邮件：每个员工每周写最重要的 5 件事，全公司可见。「让你看清楚各种公司的大小讯号」——两个团队在做一模一样的事，读 Top 5 就自然显现。老黄自己每天强迫自己读大量 email、快速做决定，「在每天不断的练习之下，看事情看得非常清楚」。英伟达因此是一个相对很透明的组织
sentences.en: Supporting mechanism — the Top 5 email: every employee writes their five most important things each week, visible to the whole company. 'It lets you see all the big and small signals of the company' — if two teams are doing exactly the same thing, reading the Top 5s makes it show up naturally. Jensen himself forces himself to read a huge amount of email every day and make decisions fast; 'through constant daily practice, he sees things very clearly.' That's why NVIDIA is a relatively very transparent organization.
sentences.note: 表达提示Top 5 email → 每周最重要的 5 件事邮件；company-wide → 全公司可见；big and small signals → 大小讯号；transparent organization → 透明的组织

sentences.cn: （引用）「Mission is the boss，而不是你的 boss。」
sentences.en: 'Mission is the boss — not your boss.'
sentences.note: 表达提示注意英文语序 mission is the boss；这句话是老黄的管理名句，常被员工转述

sentences.cn: 核心机制：英伟达从不裁员、没有末尾淘汰，只有 performance review。「人跟人之间的信任很重要——当一个员工对公司有认同感、有安全感，他愿意讲出一般在担心被淘汰的地方不愿意讲的事情。」「在全部都抢出头的地方，反而不容易促成团结合作。」
sentences.en: NVIDIA never lays people off, has no stack-ranking, only performance reviews. 'Trust between people is very important — when an employee has a sense of identification and security with the company, they're willing to say the things people at places worried about elimination wouldn't say.' 'In a place where everyone is fighting to stand out, it's actually harder to build solidarity and cooperation.'
sentences.note: 表达提示lay off → 裁员；stack-ranking → 末尾淘汰；performance review → 绩效考核；fight to stand out → 抢出头；solidarity → 团结

sentences.cn: 关键理解 · 红利与代价：红利是敢讲真话、愿意团结合作；代价是「当一项科技逐渐成熟的时候，员工需要一点时间学习新东西做转型，比直接 hire 一批已经会的人慢」——所以英伟达「不会是跑得最快的那个，但它靠的是早十年、早五年的提前布局（像 CUDA 布局了十年），对快的要求不高，但对眼光要求很高」
sentences.en: The upside and the cost: the upside is daring to speak the truth and being willing to cooperate; the cost is that 'when a technology gradually matures, employees need some time to learn new things and transition — slower than directly hiring a batch of people who already know it.' So NVIDIA 'won't be the fastest runner, but it relies on laying groundwork five to ten years early (CUDA was laid out over ten years) — it doesn't demand speed, but it demands vision.'
sentences.note: 表达提示speak the truth → 讲真话；transition → 转型；lay groundwork → 提前布局；demand vision → 对眼光要求高

sentences.cn: 真实场景：疫情期间很多公司裁员，英伟达的选择是砍 travel、砍工具（考虑不用 Slack 来省钱）——「照顾员工，一起度过困难」
sentences.en: A real example: during the pandemic, when many companies laid people off, NVIDIA's choice was to cut travel and cut tools (even considering not using Slack to save money) — 'take care of the employees and get through the hard times together.'
sentences.note: 表达提示cut travel → 砍差旅；Slack → 企业协作软件；get through the hard times → 度过困难

paraphrase.intent: 想说「任务导向而非老板导向」
phrases: At NVIDIA, the mission outranks any manager.
Your boss isn't the boss — the mission is.
paraphrase.chunks: outranks · the mission is
paraphrase.usage: 第二句是口号式转述，简洁有力；outrank 偏书面

paraphrase.intent: 想说「不裁员的组织靠信任」
phrases: No layoffs means people can afford to speak up.
Security breeds honesty; fear breeds silence.
paraphrase.chunks: afford to speak up · security breeds honesty
paraphrase.usage: 第二句对仗、适合做金句；第一句更平实

scenes.title_cn: 十、模型竞争不是鱿鱼游戏（03:12:20）
scenes.title_en: Model Competition Isn't a Squid Game
scenes.context: 从研究员的竞争心态到管理者的造市场心态，以及为什么历史上没有公司能垄断所有科技。语域：心态转变 + 行业判断。
scenes.speak: A researcher's career path is beating someone's SOTA — reviewers ask if you're state of the art, so researchers are born highly competitive: mine has to be better than yours. But once he became a manager, the mindset shifted: I don't really want to compete anymore, I've been past that stage. It's not hiding — it's confidence: what we build can genuinely help people; the goal isn't defeating rivals but making great results and putting out a better foundation so everyone can move faster. You don't have to beat your rival to make a contribution. What does war even mean? I'm not planning to kill anyone — our mindset is how to build the market. Position dictates playbook: NVIDIA doesn't play the Squid Game because it wants the whole ocean. And historically, no company has ever mastered every technology while everyone else fell behind — the software companies that survived all found a way to differentiate, and there's no reason models will be the exception.

sentences.cn: 在讲什么：研究员的毕业路径是「打败别人的 SOTA」——review 会问你是不是 state of the art，所以研究员天生是 highly competitive 的个体，「我的东西要比你强」。但当他做了管理者、站在英伟达生态的位置上，心态变了：「我不太想竞争了，我已经过那个时期。」
sentences.en: A researcher's career path is 'beating someone else's SOTA' — reviews ask if you're state of the art, so researchers are born highly competitive individuals: 'my thing has to be stronger than yours.' But once he became a manager, standing at NVIDIA's position in the ecosystem, his mindset changed: 'I don't really want to compete anymore — I've already been past that stage.'
sentences.note: 表达提示SOTA（state of the art）→ 当前最好水平；highly competitive → 竞争心很强；past that stage → 过了那个时期

sentences.cn: 关键理解：这不是隐藏，而是一种 confidence：「我们做出来的东西是可以帮助到大家的。我的目标并不是击败对手，我的目标是做出好成绩、提出更好的 foundation，让大家可以动得更快。」看到伙伴说「用你的模型之后效率提升了很多」，「这种肯定也是很好的一件事情」——「你不一定需要击败你的对手才能产生贡献」
sentences.en: This isn't hiding — it's a kind of confidence: 'what we make can genuinely help everyone. My goal isn't to defeat rivals; my goal is to produce great results and put out a better foundation, so everyone can move faster.' When a partner says 'after using your model, our efficiency went up a lot,' 'that kind of recognition is also a great thing' — 'you don't necessarily have to defeat your rival to make a contribution.'
sentences.note: 表达提示recognition → 肯定、认可；make a contribution → 产生贡献；defeat a rival → 击败对手；put out a foundation → 推出底座

sentences.cn: （引用）「什么叫战争呢？我没有打算把别人杀死。我们的心态不是想把别人给杀死，我们的心态是怎么去造市场。」
sentences.en: 'What does war even mean? I have no plan to kill others. Our mindset isn't about killing the others — our mindset is how to build the market.'
sentences.note: 表达提示build the market → 造市场；not X … but Y → 不是…而是…；对比句式要完整

sentences.cn: （引用）与其他概念的关系：从「击败别人」到「帮助别人」的转变，正是从 researcher 到 VP、从个人竞争到生态经营的必然切换
sentences.en: The shift from 'defeating others' to 'helping others' is exactly the necessary switch from researcher to VP, from personal competition to ecosystem stewardship.
sentences.note: 表达提示ecosystem stewardship → 生态经营；necessary switch → 必然切换；personal competition → 个人竞争

sentences.cn: （引用）一句话结论：位置决定打法——英伟达不参与鱿鱼游戏，因为它要的是整片海域
sentences.en: One-line takeaway: position dictates playbook — NVIDIA doesn't join the Squid Game, because what it wants is the whole ocean.
sentences.note: 表达提示position dictates playbook → 位置决定打法；Squid Game → 鱿鱼游戏；the whole ocean → 整片海域

sentences.cn: 核心机制：「纵观历史，从来没有一个公司掌握所有的科技、其他公司都无法追上——这从来没有在世界上发生过，我不觉得 AI 会是一个例外。」软件时代刚出现时会写软件的公司很少，现在大家都会写软件，「那些活下来的软件公司都是有区分方式的，没有理由模型会是例外」
sentences.en: 'Throughout history, no company has ever mastered all the technology with every other company unable to catch up — that has never happened in this world, and I don't think AI will be an exception.' When the software era first appeared, few companies could write software; now everyone can. 'The software companies that survived all found a way to differentiate — there's no reason models will be the exception.'
sentences.note: 表达提示catch up → 追上；differentiate → 做出区分；no reason … will be the exception → 没有理由…会是例外

paraphrase.intent: 想说「我不再以击败别人为目标」
phrases: I'm done with the winner-takes-all mindset.
Beating rivals stopped being the point a long time ago.
paraphrase.chunks: winner-takes-all · stopped being the point
paraphrase.usage: winner-takes-all 是行业术语「赢家通吃」；第二句更口语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「模型领域不会出现垄断」
phrases: No single player will ever own AI.
Models will converge, and differentiation is how you survive.
paraphrase.chunks: own AI · differentiation is how you survive
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白有力；第二句在判断之外给出生存解法

scenes.context: 本期避坑总结：与巨头硬拼的致命错误与研究员的 high ego 陷阱。语域：总结 + 方法论。
scenes.speak: If you start a company today doing exactly what OpenAI and Anthropic do, that's dangerous: your funding will never match theirs, they have no customer moat to defend, they make things cheap, and you can't easily catch up. The fix is to find pain points they can't solve — not because they don't want to, but because they can't justify why they should. Direction is fatal when wrong: the harder you work, the more you lose. The second trap is the researcher's ego: in some sense, researchers all have very high egos and think their own idea is better than everyone else's, so they get hooked on 'my algorithm beats yours' and forget what the company wants. The fix: before starting a research project, answer two questions at once — is it cutting-edge, and why does it connect to our business? Both answers are required.

sentences.cn: 原因：在已经拥挤的赛道上跟资源比你大十倍的公司硬拼——「你的资金绝对没有他们雄厚，他们没有客户壁垒，他们把东西做便宜，你不容易追上」
sentences.en: Why: head-to-head with a company ten times your resources on an already crowded track — 'your funding will never be as strong as theirs; they don't have customer moats to protect, they make things cheap, and you can't easily catch up.'
sentences.note: 表达提示head-to-head → 硬碰硬；crowded track → 拥挤的赛道；customer moat → 客户壁垒

sentences.cn: 解法：去找「他们没办法解」的痛点——不是他们不想解，是他们不能 justify 为什么要去解
sentences.en: Fix: find the pain points they 'can't solve' — it's not that they don't want to solve them, it's that they can't justify why they should.
sentences.note: 表达提示pain point → 痛点；justify → 论证合理性；not that … it's that … → 不是…而是…

sentences.cn: 严重程度：致命——方向错了，努力越大损失越大
sentences.en: Severity: fatal — get the direction wrong, and the more you work, the more you lose.
sentences.note: 表达提示fatal → 致命；the more … the more … → 越…越…

sentences.cn: （引用）嘉宾说法：「如果你现在开一间公司，要跟 OpenAI、Anthropic 做一样的事情，很危险。」
sentences.en: 'If you start a company today doing the same thing as OpenAI and Anthropic, that's very dangerous.'
sentences.note: 表达提示do the same thing as → 做和…一样的事情；start a company → 开公司

sentences.cn: 原因：「研究员某方面来讲都是 very high ego，每个人都觉得自己想法比别人好」——这让人沉迷于「我的算法比你强」，却忘了公司要的是「这对公司为什么重要」
sentences.en: Why: 'in some sense researchers all have very high egos — everyone thinks their own idea is better than everyone else's' — that hooks people on 'my algorithm is stronger than yours', and makes them forget what the company wants: 'why is this important to the company?'
sentences.note: 表达提示high ego → 自我很强；get hooked on → 沉迷于；algorithm → 算法

sentences.cn: 解法：研究立项时同时回答两个问题：它是不是前沿？它和公司的生意为什么相关？——两个答案缺一不可
sentences.en: Fix: when starting a research project, answer two questions at the same time: is it cutting-edge? And why is it relevant to the company's business? — both answers are indispensable.
sentences.note: 表达提示cutting-edge → 前沿；relevant to the business → 与生意相关；indispensable → 缺一不可

paraphrase.intent: 想说「别在别人的主场硬拼」
phrases: Don't fight a bigger dog on its own turf.
You can't out-resource them, so don't try — pick a different fight.
paraphrase.chunks: on its own turf · pick a different fight
paraphrase.usage: fight on its own turf 是惯用比喻；pick a different fight 是行动建议，更口语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「研究要同时回答前沿与相关」
phrases: Frontier without business relevance is just a hobby.
A project needs both novelty and a reason to exist.
paraphrase.chunks: just a hobby · a reason to exist
paraphrase.usage: hobby 的贬义对比很强；reason to exist 简洁准确

practice.cn: 用「picks and shovels」说：英伟达卖铲子，不挖金矿。
practice.en: NVIDIA sells the picks and shovels — it powers solution companies instead of being one.

practice.cn: 用「zero-billion-dollar business」说：现在不赚钱，成功后极其有影响力。
practice.en: Cosmos is a zero-billion-dollar business — no revenue today, wildly influential if it lands.

practice.cn: 用「mission is the boss」说：任务比任何经理都大。
practice.en: At NVIDIA, mission is the boss — the mission outranks any manager.

practice.cn: 用「align」说：立项前先让兴趣与公司利益对齐。
practice.en: Before starting any project, align your interest with the company's business.

pitfalls.right: NVIDIA is a computing company — it helps the companies that build solutions succeed.
pitfalls.why: 把英伟达说成 solution 公司就丢了核心定位；用 computing company + helps … succeed 的对照才准确。

pitfalls.wrong: I want to ask my boss for 1000 A100 GPUs.
pitfalls.right: To win GPUs, explain why your work impacts the problem the company is solving.
pitfalls.why: 要 GPU 不是「要」而是「证明相关性」；用 explain the impact / align 说清机制，才能体现访谈精髓。

pitfalls.right: NVIDIA never lays people off and has no stack-ranking.
pitfalls.why: 「裁员」英语说 fire / lay off，不是 cut person；「末尾淘汰」是 stack-ranking，二者含义不同。

pitfalls.wrong: Our mindset is not killing others, our mindset is making market.
pitfalls.right: Our mindset isn't about killing competitors — it's about building the market.
pitfalls.why: make market 是中式说法；英语说 build / grow the market。并列对比用 it's not A — it's B 更地道。

shifts.before: 以为做研究就是比谁的算法在榜单上更强
shifts.after: 研究员立项前也先回答「这为什么对公司重要」——兴趣与公司利益对齐

shifts.before: 以为产品/模型的 SKU 越多越全能
shifts.after: 备多则力寡——从 22 个模型收敛到一个 Omni 模型，少即是多

shifts.before: 以为 AI 竞争是鱿鱼游戏式的零和博弈
shifts.after: 造市场而非存量竞争——不击败对手也能产生贡献，英伟达要的是整片海域
